explanation: Single EXCLURAD (eta configuration) input file covering the requested scan: W=1.6 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV2, cos(theta*)=0, phi* stepped uniformly from 0 to 345 deg in 25 points (step = 345/24 = 14.375 deg). All 25 points share the same W, Q2, cos(theta*) and only phi* varies, per the exclurad.F reader convention (npoi given once, followed by four length-N arrays: W, Q2, cos(theta*), phi*). Although the eta/README.md states a 10-point-per-file Fortran reader limit, the source (exclurad.F lines 18-54) declares npoimax=10000 and the shipped eta/examples/input_multi_chunk.dat itself demonstrates a working 50-point single-call file with values wrapped across multiple rows -- confirming N=25 requires no chunking into multiple exclurad.exe invocations. Used model=3 (maid2000/EtaMAID2023), ivec=1 (recoil proton), bmom=6.535 GeV (matching the repo's default input.dat / CLAS12 beam energy), vcut=0.166 GeV^2 (standard CLAS12 eta inelasticity cut), lepton=1, rc_mode=0 (full O(alpha) corrections). The kinematic point (W=1.6 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV2, cos theta*=0) lies safely above the eta production threshold (W_thr ~ 1.4859 GeV) and well inside the EtaMAID-2023 table grid (Q2 in [0,5] GeV2, W in [1.4856,6] GeV per mpintp.inc), so no unphysical or out-of-table points are expected in this run.
